AC:
- `todo.py search` ranks by IDF-weighted term overlap: a term present in nearly
  every todo contributes ~nothing to the score, a rare term dominates. The old
  substring-plus-0.1-per-token ranker is gone, not merely supplemented.
- Morphological variants match: `embedding` finds "embeddings", `merge` finds
  "merging", and "class"/"pass" are not truncated to "clas"/"pas".
- The stemming hook is ONE documented seam, exercised by a test that swaps in an
  alternate stemmer without editing any call site.
- Stopwords are derived from corpus IDF against a stated threshold, persisted in
  `<todo-dir>/config.json`, and reused on the next run. No hardcoded English
  stopword list ships. Hand-editing the config list is honored.
- `clear search data` (name per the ALL-sentinel convention) drops the derived
  index for a selector or `ALL`; the next `search` re-derives what it needs
  lazily and returns the same results as before the clear.
- With the off switch set in `<todo-dir>/config.json`, `search` runs with zero
  embedders: no Apple NLCE sidecar is spawned, no vectors are written, and
  results come from FTS/IDF alone. `--embedder <name>` still overrides it
  explicitly, and `todo.py embedders` still lists the registered backends.
- Tests: IDF ranking order, de-pluralization/de-gerunding, stopword discovery
  and persistence, clear-then-re-derive round trip, and the off switch (asserting
  the embedder is never instantiated). Existing search/embedder tests still pass.
- The three open design questions in the Body are answered in the Body (or in
  the docs) before implementation starts, not left to the implementer.
ActualSummary: Landed as planned in seven sequential chunks with no subtodos and no descopes. The IDF ranker replaced the substring lexical ranker outright and fused as ONE ranking over all terms rather than one per term -- RRF is rank-based, so the per-term shape discarded the IDF magnitudes and let a common-only match tie a rare one. Two behaviors emerged during the work and are now the contract: matching only a discovered stopword is not matching (a stopword-only hit is absent, not merely ranked lower), and clear-search-data recomputes the stopword list against the corpus as it stands rather than restoring what was cleared, which is how a stale list gets corrected. The embedder config key was implemented as a full selector (null = off, name or list = select) rather than an off-switch-only flag, following the key's own framing. Verified on the real corpus: discovery found English function words plus the domain words 'todo' and 'model' with no shipped list. 548 tests pass.

Body.raw:
Give `todo.py search` a real full-text search ranker, weighted by IDF over the
todo corpus, and make the vector (embedding) side optional rather than mandatory.

Today's lexical ranker is a placeholder (todo.py:1774-1784 in search_tickets):
a whole-term substring hit scores 1.0, and each whitespace token present in the
concatenated raws adds 0.1. No term is weighted by how common it is, so "todo",
"work", "search" and "the" all count exactly as much as a rare distinguishing
term. It is fused by RRF alongside the per-embedder rankers, so a corpus-wide
word can drag an irrelevant todo up the list.

Five pieces:

1. Tokenizer + normalizer, WITH A STEMMING HOOK.
   One documented seam (a function or small protocol) that maps a raw token to
   its index form, so a Porter/Snowball stemmer -- or a real morphological
   analyzer -- can be dropped in later without touching any caller. For now the
   hook is implemented as deliberately simple morphology only:
     - de-pluralization: trailing "s"/"es", leaving "ss" alone
     - de-gerunding: trailing "ing"
   Nothing cleverer. The point of this pass is the seam, not the linguistics.

2. IDF index over the corpus.
   Document frequency per normalized term across every todo's embeddable raws
   (Summary, Body, and each Tag element -- the same target list _embed_targets
   already walks). Query terms score by IDF-weighted overlap so a rare term
   dominates and a near-universal one contributes ~nothing. Keep it as a
   ranking that joins the existing RRF fusion, replacing the naive lexical
   ranker rather than being bolted next to it.

3. Stopwords DISCOVERED ALGORITHMICALLY, not hardcoded.
   A term whose IDF falls below a threshold is a stopword by definition of this
   corpus -- which correctly catches the domain words a shipped English list
   would miss ("todo", "work item", "sha", "branch", "commit"). The discovered
   set is collected into the per-todo-dir `<todo-dir>/config.json` -- the same
   config that already carries `todo_storage` and `default_state_filter`, read
   via todo_store.config_value / _load_config -- so it is inspectable, editable
   by hand, and stable between runs instead of being recomputed every search.
   Decide (and write down) how the threshold is expressed and when the set is
   refreshed.

4. `clear search data` command.
   The index is DERIVED data, exactly like embeddings: droppable at any time
   with nothing lost, and re-derived lazily on the next search -- the same
   contract the vector path already has (search backfills missing vectors
   in-line, printing "refreshing embeddings..."). The store abstraction already
   exposes the analogous surface for vectors (todo_store: clear_embeddings /
   put_embedding / all_embeddings / embeddings_for_ticket, both backends), so
   model the FTS index on it. Selector should follow the ALL convention
   (`<selector>` or the `ALL` sentinel) like doctor / log / tag-clear.

5. Repo config to turn the embedded (vector) search OFF.
   A `<todo-dir>/config.json` key that makes the embedder set empty for this
   store -- "embedder == None" -- so `search` runs FTS/IDF alone: no Apple NLCE
   sidecar spawn, no lazy vector backfill, no all-zero-vector failure mode. This
   is what makes the FTS path usable standalone (fast, hermetic, no macOS
   dependency), and it is a store-level policy, not a per-invocation flag, so
   `--embedder` still overrides explicitly when asked. Note the existing hidden
   `null` backend is a DIFFERENT thing (an embedder that returns a degenerate
   vector); this config should skip the embedder loop entirely rather than
   selecting a no-op embedder.

DECISIONS RATIFIED IN GROOMING (2026-08-12):

  - INDEX STORAGE: no persisted per-todo lexical index. Tokenize the corpus
    fresh on every search (a few hundred records is milliseconds) and persist
    only the corpus-level document-frequency / stopword table. No index schema
    bump, no write-path invalidation, no file-dir backend mirroring. The
    asymmetry with vectors is deliberate: embedding is expensive and lexical
    tokenizing is not, so only the expensive artifact earns storage.

  - CLEAR SCOPE: `clear search data` drops BOTH sides -- the lexical/IDF derived
    data and the stored embedding vectors -- and everything re-derives lazily on
    the next search. Given the storage decision above, what it concretely
    removes is the corpus-level stats table plus the vectors; there is no
    per-todo lexical index to drop.

  - STOPWORDS ARE DERIVED TOO: clearing also drops the discovered stopword set
    from config.json, and the next search rediscovers it. Consequence, accepted:
    hand-edits to that list do NOT survive a clear.

  - COMMAND NAME: `clear-search-data`, kebab-case like `tag-clear` and
    `migrate-to-latest`, taking `<selector>|ALL` like `doctor` / `log` /
    `tag-clear`. Picked as the codebase-conventional default; the user's answer
    on this point was cut off mid-sentence ("both, and I think the command ..."),
    so if they meant something else about the command, this is the line to change.

TRACKER: sequential WorkItems on ONE branch, no subtodos. This is a single
subsystem (the search path in todo.py plus its config), one actor, and the
chunks are strictly ordered -- tokenizer before ranker before stopwords before
the clear command. Nothing here wants its own END test or review boundary, so
per `frequentcommits` none of it earns a sub-branch.

Related prior art in the corpus: todo:83cd1c8f (vec search command),
todo:a31d8f24 (vec search ranking), todo:91e28fd0 (unsupervised semantic term
vocabulary from corpus -- the successor that would re-arm automatic tagging).
Auto-tagging is currently dormant because the removed `hash` backend was purely
lexical collision noise; an IDF ranker is NOT a revival of that -- it is honest
lexical matching in its own lane, fused with, or standing in for, the semantic
one.

LongSummary.raw:
Adds honest lexical search to todo.py: an IDF-weighted full-text ranker over the todo corpus, replacing the placeholder lexical ranker in search_tickets that scored a substring hit at 1.0 and each present whitespace token at 0.1, weighting no term by how common it is. Query terms are normalized through a tokenizer with a deliberate stemming seam -- v1 does trailing s/es de-pluralization (leaving ss alone) and -ing de-gerunding, nothing cleverer, so a real Porter or Snowball stemmer can be dropped in later without touching a caller.

Stopwords are discovered from the corpus rather than shipped: any term whose IDF falls below a threshold is a stopword by definition of this corpus, which catches the domain words an English list would miss -- todo, work item, sha, branch, commit. The discovered set is persisted in the per-todo-dir config.json beside todo_storage and default_state_filter.

Two lifecycle pieces come with it. A clear-search-data command drops the derived search artifacts -- the corpus statistics, the stopword set, and the stored embedding vectors -- with everything re-derived lazily on the next search, the same contract the vector path already has when it backfills missing vectors in-line. And a store-level config key empties the embedder set, the embedder == None case, so search runs on FTS and IDF alone with no Apple NLCE sidecar spawn, no vector backfill, and no all-zero-vector failure mode; --embedder still overrides explicitly.

Ratified in grooming: no persisted per-todo lexical index (tokenize fresh each search, persist only corpus-level statistics), clear drops both the lexical and vector sides, and the stopword set is derived data that a clear also drops, so hand-edits to it are not durable. The work is sequential WorkItems on one branch -- one subsystem, no subtodos.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): tokenizer with a stemming seam

The lexical side of search needs one place that turns text into index terms, and
a future real stemmer needs somewhere to plug in that is not 'edit every caller'.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_search.py: new module. STEMMER is the seam --
a module attribute read at call time, so rebinding it swaps the algorithm and
nothing else moves. The shipped stem() is deliberately crude and idempotent:
de-pluralize (-es only after a sibilant, so 'notes' does not become 'not'; never
after 'ss', so 'class' survives), de-gerund (-ing, refused when the stem would be
shorter than 4, so 'thing' survives), then drop a trailing 'e' on words of 5+.
That last rule is what makes 'merge' and 'merging' both land on 'merg' -- the
case the substring ranker could not do at all. Also lands the IDF and stopword
helpers the next two chunks consume.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search.py: unit tests for each rule,
idempotency across the lot, and a seam test that swaps in a different stemmer
via patch and asserts tokenize() picks it up with no call-site change.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Tokenizer + normalizer with the stemming SEAM: one documented function/protocol mapping a raw token to its index form. v1 morphology only -- trailing s/es de-pluralization leaving ss alone, trailing -ing de-gerunding. Unit tests including a swapped-in alternate stemmer that touches no call site.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): rank lexical search by IDF instead of substring hits

The old lexical ranker weighted no term by how common it was -- a whole-term
substring hit scored 1.0 and each present whitespace token added 0.1 -- so
'todo' or 'search' counted as much as a rare distinguishing word and could drag
an irrelevant todo up the fused ranking.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_search.py: LexicalIndex builds a fresh IDF
view of the corpus per search and scores all terms into ONE ranking (their
weights add) rather than one ranking per term -- RRF is rank-based, so splitting
per term threw the IDF magnitudes away and let a common-only match tie a rare
one. Keeps two properties the old ranker had by accident and the tests depend
on: a contiguous phrase beats the same words scattered (an explicit bonus, since
IDF cannot see word order), and a document matching nothing is absent rather
than scored zero. Adds a weight floor so a term in EVERY todo still returns
them, and skips stopwords unless the whole query is stopwords -- judged across
the query, not per term, or 'the quokka' would reinstate 'the'.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py: search_tickets uses it; the substring
block is gone.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search.py: ranking order, phrase bonus,
absent-when-no-match, universal-term floor, the stopword fallback boundary, and
morphological matching. Full suite 533 passed.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] IDF ranker: document frequency per normalized term over every todo's embeddable raws (Summary, Body, each Tag element -- the _embed_targets list), scoring query terms by IDF-weighted overlap. Replaces the substring+0.1-per-token ranker in search_tickets and joins the existing RRF fusion. Unit tests on ranking order.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): discover stopwords from the corpus into config.json

A shipped English stopword list is the wrong list for this corpus: the words
that carry no signal here are 'todo', 'sha', 'branch', 'commit'. So nobody
writes one -- a term earns the label by falling below an IDF threshold, which
is a property of the corpus rather than of English.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py: resolve_stopwords() reads the persisted
list or discovers and writes one, lazily and stickily -- the same contract as
the embedding backfill beside it, so a hand-edited list is honored rather than
recomputed behind the user's back and clear-search-data is how you ask for a
fresh one. --dry-run discovers without writing. Adds the config keys
search_stopwords / search_stopword_min_idf (default 0.3, i.e. a term in ~74%+ of
todos) and the embedder key the next chunk uses.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_store.py: config_float / config_list /
config_has / update_config. update_config is read-modify-write so touching one
key never clobbers the storage DSN; config_has exists because a key set to null
must be distinguishable from an absent key -- that is how the off switch says
OFF rather than unspecified.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_search.py: use_stopwords(), because
discovery needs a built index -- build, discover, then adopt.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search.py: CLI tests for discovery,
persistence, a hand-edited list surviving, --dry-run writing nothing, and the
threshold being configurable. 29 passed.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Stopword discovery: terms below an IDF threshold become stopwords, persisted to <todo-dir>/config.json next to todo_storage/default_state_filter. Decide and document how the threshold is expressed and when the set refreshes; honor a hand-edited list. Unit tests on discovery + persistence + reuse.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): config switch to run search without any embedder

The only production embedder needs a macOS Swift sidecar, so on a machine that
cannot build it every search either fails or pays for a subprocess it did not
want. With a real lexical ranker in place, vectors become optional.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py: resolve_embedder_names() reads the
store's 'embedder' config key -- absent means every non-hidden embedder (today's
behavior), null means NONE so lexical IDF is the only ranker, and a name or list
selects. Null skips instantiation entirely, so no sidecar spawns and no vector is
backfilled. Interpreting a non-null value as a selection follows the key's own
framing (embedder == None is off, so embedder == 'apple' is that one); a value
of neither shape errors rather than silently falling back to the default.
--embedder always wins, since it is the explicit ask.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo_store.py: config_value_raw, needed because
every other reader coerces and this one must see null as a value.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search.py: the off switch proven the
hard way -- the sidecar binary is pointed at a nonexistent path, so any attempt
to embed would fail and success means nothing tried -- plus the flag override,
a named embedder, the untouched default, and the error on a nonsense value.
34 passed.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] Embedder off switch: a config.json key that empties the embedder set for this store (embedder == None), so search runs FTS/IDF alone with no sidecar spawn and no vector backfill. --embedder still overrides explicitly; embedders still lists backends. Test asserts no embedder is instantiated.

WorkItems.message:
feat(todo): clear-search-data drops what search derived

Derived data needs a way to be thrown away, or a stale artifact is permanent.
This is the counterpart to lazy derivation: search backfills what is missing,
and this removes what is there.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py: clear-search-data <selector>|ALL removes
embedding vectors from BOTH copies (the embeddings index and the vectors stamped
into the ticket JSON -- clearing only the index would leave search reading the
record's) and, on ALL only, the discovered stopword list from config.json, since
that list is a property of the corpus and not of any one todo. Writes with
no_clear because the raws did not change. The lexical index is deliberately not
mentioned: it is never stored, so there is nothing to clear.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search.py: both copies of the vectors
going, re-derive restoring them exactly, a single-todo clear leaving the corpus
list alone, and the required selector.

skills/projectmanagement/todos/test_todo_search_idf.py: two END-gate assertions
corrected against behavior that is deliberate and unit-tested rather than the
other way round. A todo matching ONLY a discovered stopword now must be absent,
not merely ranked lower -- matching only a stopword is not matching. And after a
clear the list is recomputed from the corpus as it stands, so a word in 9 of 13
todos is correctly no longer a stopword though it was at 9 of 10; the gate now
asserts that fresh recomputation instead of expecting the old list back, which
is the more useful property. END gate passes.
WorkItems.summary: [MIDCAP] clear-search-data <selector>|ALL: drop the derived search data -- corpus stats, stopword set, and stored embedding vectors -- with lazy re-derive on the next search. Follows the ALL-sentinel convention of doctor/log/tag-clear. Tests on the clear-then-re-derive round trip.
